newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS CHARGE PAST CELTICS FOR 6-0 START.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS CHARGE PAST CELTICS FOR 6-0 START.

text.p: The Chicago Bulls took a while to make their charge but led by the incomparable Michael Jordan they found their stride and ran over the Boston Celtics 104-92 Saturday to ensure their best season start ever.
Jordan scored 27 points over three quarters and Scottie Pippen finished one point shy of a triple-double for the Bulls, who moved out to a 6-0 start, eclipsing last season's franchise record.
Pippen had nine points, 11 assists and 12 rebounds, and Toni Kukoc added 21 points off the bench.
"I'm not sure if we could be as good as last year," said Bulls back-up centre Bill Wennington. "But I know this team likes to win and hates to lose."

The Bulls led by just four at the half and trailed 55-54, two minutes into the third period. Jordan then supplied half the points in a 16-4 spurt that gave Chicago the lead for good at 70-59 with 4:28 to play in the quarter.
Todd Day tallied 20 points for the Celtics.
"That's why they are the world champions," said Boston coach M.L. Carr. "They can come out and look lousy for a couple of quarters and still find some way to beat you."
In Houston, Hakeem Olajuwon overcame foul trouble to score 17 of his 38 points in the fourth quarter as the unbeaten Rockets beat the Utah Jazz 91-85 for their sixth straight win.
The Rockets, who matched Chicago with a 6-0 start, trailed 65-62 entering the fourth quarter but took the lead for good at 75-74 on a three-pointer by Matt Bullard with 5:25 left.
Olajuwon scored Houston's next 12 points on four baskets and four free throws, providing the Rockets with an 87-81 lead with under three minutes to go.
The Jazz clawed back to 90-85 with 2:12 left, but Utah never scored again.
Karl Malone scored a season-high 32 points for the Jazz, who were playing for the first time since Monday.

In Charlotte, Vin Baker scored nine of his 28 points in the fourth quarter, including a tie-breaking, three-point play with 1:28 remaining to lift the Milwaukee Bucks to a 100-98 victory over the Charlotte Hornets.
The Hornets tied it at 96-96 on Matt Geiger's basket with 1:46 to go. But 18 seconds later, Baker made a short jumper and was fouled. His free throw gave the Bucks a 99-96 edge.
Geiger stole the ball in the dying seconds but Glen Rice missed a possible game-winning three-pointer as the Bucks prevailed for the fourth time in their last five games.
Anthony Mason led the Hornets with 21 points.
At Indiana, Travis Best scored 23 points and Antonio Davis had 20 and 11 rebounds as the Pacers broke into the win column with a 103-100 overtime win over the Washington Bullets.

Washington led 88-81 with under four minutes to play in regulation before Best scored six in a 13-4 run that gave Indiana a 94-92 lead with 5.4 seconds left. But Rod Strickland drove in for a layup at the buzzer to force overtime.

In the extra session, Chris Webber's hook gave Washington a 96-94 advantage before Davis and Reggie Miller hit jumpers and Dale Davis made a layup for a 100-96 lead and the Bullets never came closer than two points thereafter.
Miller netted 16 points for the Pacers, who prevented their first 0-4 start since 1988.
In Philadelphia, Jerry Stackhouse scored 36 points, including 21 in the first half when the 76ers raced to a 27-point lead, to help Philadelphia to a 112-95 victory over the winless Phoenix Suns.

Derrick Coleman and Mark Davis scored 14 points apiece for the 76ers, who beat the Suns for the first time in 11 games dating to February 1, 1991. Philadelphia has won two straight games after opening the season with three losses.
Michael Finley scored 25 points for the Suns (0-5).
In Sacramento, Lionel Simmons hit two free throws with 3.8 seconds remaining to complete a closing 14-4 run and lift the Kings to a 103-102 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.

After Portland's Arvydas Sabonis made two free throws for a 102-101 advantage with 5.9 seconds left, Sacramento lined up to inbound the ball. Portland's Clifford Robinson tipped the pass, but fouled Simmons in pursuit of the loose ball.
Portland had a chance to win it, but Kenny Anderson's one-hander from inside the paint bounced off the front of the rim. Anderson beat Minnesota in similar fashion on Wednesday.
Mitch Richmond scored 12 of his 29 points for Sacramento during the final three minutes. Sabonis had 22 points and 13 rebounds for Portland.
In Dallas, Alonzo Mourning scored six of his 11 points in the final three minutes as the Miami Heat continued their dominance of the Dallas Mavericks with a 91-84 victory.
The Heat, who have beaten the Mavericks 10 consecutive times, took advantage of horrendous foul shooting down the stretch by Dallas, who missed 9-of-20 free throws overall.
Dan Maerle and Tim Hardaway led the Heat with 19 points each, while Jamal Mashburn had 19 for Dallas.
